title: osf bumps agnix-core 0.54.0 → 0.56.1
summary: A dependency-only change: the `osf` crate pins `agnix-core` from `=0.54.0` to `=0.56.1`, and Cargo.lock follows with the matching `agnix-core` 0.56.1 and its transitive `agnix-rules` 0.56.5. No source in this repository changes; the blast radius is whatever `osf` does with the agnix linting API, since the crate is pinned exactly and the lockfile is the only place the resolved graph is recorded.

nodes.label: osf

nodes.label: osf Cargo.toml
nodes.subtitle: agnix-core = "=0.56.1"
nodes.summary: Declares an exact-version pin on agnix-core. The `=` prefix means the resolved version cannot drift within the 0.56 line; the bump is deliberate and total.

nodes.label: Cargo.lock
nodes.subtitle: resolved versions + checksums
nodes.summary: Records the concrete resolved graph: agnix-core 0.56.1 and agnix-rules 0.56.5, each with a new checksum. This is the artifact that makes the build reproducible.

nodes.label: agnix-core
nodes.summary: The linting engine osf depends on. Two minor versions of upstream change arrive at once; the API surface osf calls is the thing to check against the upstream changelog.

nodes.label: agnix-rules
nodes.summary: Transitive dependency of agnix-core, carrying the rule definitions. It moves independently of agnix-core's own version, so rule behaviour can change even where the core API does not.

edges.summary: The one line that actually changed in this repository: the exact pin on agnix-core.
osf's build reads its manifest to resolve dependencies; unchanged, but it is why the pin matters to this crate.
Cargo re-resolved the constraint and rewrote the lockfile entries and checksums.
agnix-core pulls agnix-rules; both moved, and the rules crate landed on a different patch version than the core.
The unchanged call path from osf into the linting engine — the surface where a 0.54→0.56 API change would break the build.
